app.title: Phylogenetic Tree Generator (DNA Clustering with K-mers)
app.summary: A person uploads several FASTA files, one per species, picks a k-mer size and one of three distance measures in a settings sidebar, and runs the pipeline. The interface shows a summary table of each sequence's length and count of unique k-mers, a pairwise distance matrix, and a UPGMA dendrogram built from that matrix. The person can change k or the measure and run again to see how the tree shifts, then download the matrix with its summary as a CSV and the dendrogram as a PNG.

task.text: Compare whole DNA sequences without aligning them, by their k-mer profiles, and cluster them into a tree of relationships.

data.text: A set of whole DNA sequences, one per file, turned into normalised k-mer frequency profiles, a square matrix of pairwise distances, and a tree clustered from it.
data.item: one species' DNA sequence from a FASTA file

stage.text: analysing relationships among downloaded sequences, before writing up the tree

mechanism.text: A sidebar holds the file upload, the k-mer size, the distance method and a run button that only runs once files and a method are chosen; running it fills the main area with a summary table, a distance matrix and a dendrogram, all recomputed from the same settings. Download buttons for the matrix CSV and the dendrogram PNG appear once results are kept in the session.

field.text: alignment-free sequence comparison with k-mer profiles in phylogenetics

workflow.name: compute pairwise distances between items and cluster them into a tree

steps.here: Several .fasta or .fa files are uploaded in the sidebar; each file is one species, named after the file, with header lines dropped and the sequence uppercased.

steps.step: set the parameters of the computation
steps.here: A number input sets k (2–15, recommended 5–8, with a warning below 5) and a dropdown picks manhattan, jaccard or cosine; an expandable guide explains what each choice favours, and the run button warns if no method or no files are given.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each sequence is broken into overlapping k-mers whose counts are normalised to frequencies; a summary table lists each species' length in bp and its number of unique k-mers.
The chosen measure is applied to every pair of profiles and the full square matrix is shown to three decimals.
The matrix is clustered by average linkage (UPGMA) and drawn as a right-facing dendrogram titled with k and the method, branches coloured below 70% of the highest merge.
One CSV holds the method and k as comment lines, the sequence summary and the distance matrix; a second button saves the dendrogram as a PNG.

distinctive: No alignment step: sequences are compared only through their k-mer frequency profiles.
Three distance measures with different meanings (presence/absence of k-mers, frequency differences, composition pattern), and the interface warns that the choice of measure and k changes the tree.
The k-mer size is checked against a recommended range, with a warning that small k loses specificity.
The exported CSV records the method and k in its header, so runs with different settings can be told apart and compared.
